 What Morgan Gibbs-White did after Elliot Anderson was sent off for England
 Lee Clarke
 Sun 15 November 2026 21:45 GMT · 1 min read Add to Preferred Sources Photo by Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images Add to Preferred Sources 
 England played their part in an unbelievable contest as they clung on to beat Spain 3-2 and reach the semi-final of the Nations League. 
 Anderson pulled back Lamine Yamal after some dreadful defending from Jarrel Quansah as England pressed the self-destruct button inside the Metropolitano in Madrid. 
 The red card for Anderson smashed any chance of Gibbs-White adding another cap to his collection, but he was spotted helping his former club teammate in another fashion.

 What Morgan Gibbs-White did after Elliot Anderson got sent off vs Spain
 Anderson had to wait for a pretty quick VAR check to be completed to determine whether or not there was a foul in the build-up to the decision to award Yamal a penalty. 
 Once Anderson had been confirmed as being sent off. Gibbs-White stepped off the bench and gave his former Forest teammate a big embrace, with the midfielder looking gutted at what had happened. 
 It was a lovely touch from the Forest number 10 with Anderson facing up to the possible consequence of his decision to haul down Yamal and turn the game in the favour of Spain. 
 Gibbs-White will be gutted not to get on the pitch again during another England game, but ultimately it was a case of needs must, as the Three Lions had a lead to preserve, which they did valiantly. 
 The fact he was the first player to step off the bench and check on Anderson after his disappointment suggests what kind of leader he is and dispels any theory that he’s not a good Forest captain.
